text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- One of Malaysia's top corporate figures, Yahaya Ahmad, and wife killed in helicopter crash in Pahang.
- People's Action Party leaders apply for opposition politician Tang Liang Hong's defences in 12 defamation cases to be struck off.
- Anti-smoking committee wants to increase tobacco taxes as way to curb smoking.
- Computer company IPC Corp selling six percent stake to Sungwoo Group for Singapore $39.6 million.
- Thai finance and banking shares dive.
- Death of Yahaya Ahmad in helicopter crash raises concerns over future direction of 13 listed companies in Malaysia and Singapore with market value of Malaysian $40 million.
- Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan says most likely prospect for U.S. economy is sustainable growth.
- Listed IPC Corp group in Singapore $39.6 million deal that will help IPC salvage its troubled Korean operations.
- Bondholders of Amcol Holdings may get guarantee from Sinar Mas Group.
- Aztech Systems to provide in its 1996 accounts for damages from copyright infringement suit with Creative Technology Ltd.
- Small investors will get 41.6 percent of shares in Omni Industries' public offering.
- Pentex Schweizer Circuits announces it is acquiring Degussa Electronics for Singapore $47.5 million to create $180 million printed circuit board group.
